authority.primary_identity: Scan of the printed SPI folio, 'Second Edition Copyright 1971, Simulations Publications Inc.' printed on the map sheet (page 5).

method: Every correction was re-read from the folio scan before being applied. Pages were extracted at native scan resolution (no rasterisation dpi applied, no resampling of the source), cropped as fractional boxes, rotated where the print is rotated, upscaled by LANCZOS where needed, opened as images and read BY EYE, then independently cross-checked with Tesseract 5 --psm 6 over the same crop file. Eye and OCR agreed on every correction applied. Counting claims were verified twice, by naw_locate.py word search at all four rotations and by whole-block visual inventory.

severity_legend.critical: an unchecked obligation or a legality-changing trigger; a gate built on the uncorrected text would be wrong
severity_legend.high: materially changes what the engine may or must do
severity_legend.moderate: authorises or forbids an action the folio does not, without changing a result
severity_legend.low: no effect on meaning; matters as a class or as an inventory fact

corrections.rule_ref: 2nd Ed p.5, RETREAT AND ADVANCE AS A RESULT OF COMBAT, final paragraph (British/Prussian aid, printed at 90 deg)
corrections.class: unchecked obligation - printed rule missing entirely
corrections.was: (absent) The Optional-advance paragraph ended at 'The option must be exercised immediately, is never compulsory, is limited to one hex, and costs no Movement Points.' No paragraph of the document carried the prohibition.
corrections.now: Advances are useful in cutting off the line of retreat of Enemy units whose combat has yet to be resolved. Advancing units may not participate in another attack or defense in the Combat Phase in which they advance, even if their advance places them next to Enemy units whose battles are yet to be resolved.
corrections.folio_verbatim: Advances are useful in cutting off the line of retreat of Enemy units whose combat has yet to be resolved. Advancing units may not participate in another attack or defense in the Combat Phase in which they advance, even if their advance places them next to Enemy units whose battles are yet to be resolved.

evidence.crop_spec: page 5, frac x 0.000-0.215, y 0.400-0.660, rotate 90; paragraph re-cropped alone at 2x

corrections.gate_consequence: Exempts an advanced unit from the p.1 COMBAT case (B.) obligation 'ALL Friendly units adjacent to Enemy units MUST participate in an attack' for that Combat Phase, and from being counted as a defender. Applies to the phasing player after Dr/DE/EX and to the non-phasing player after Ar. The folio does not reconcile the two obligations; that reconciliation is a register question.

corrections.rule_ref: 2nd Ed p.1 col.2, THE MAP, case (B.) [rules_2nd_ed.json MAP-04]
corrections.class: silent normalisation of a printed typo, inside quotation marks
corrections.was: A given hex is considered to be a specific type of terrain if all or any part of it contains that terrain feature symbol.
corrections.now: (B.) A given hex is considered to be a specific type of terrain if all or any part or it contains that terrain feature symbol.
corrections.folio_verbatim: A given hex is considered to be a specific type of terrain if all or any part or it contains that terrain feature symbol.

evidence.corroboration: The folio's own TEC footnote on p.5 prints the same construction correctly: 'A hex is considered to be Woods terrain if all or any part of it contains the symbol of that terrain.' That is what makes the page-1 'or' a typo and not a variant.

corrections.gate_consequence: None on meaning. Registered as a printed defect (typographical), same class as NAW2-SD-1.

corrections.rule_ref: 2nd Ed p.1 col.7, ARTILLERY, case (C) [rules_2nd_ed.json ART-09/ART-11]
corrections.was: Bombarding artillery is never eliminated or retreated by an adverse result (it may retreat voluntarily, and may voluntarily accept an 'Attacker Retreat').
corrections.now: Bombarding artillery is never eliminated or retreated by an adverse result - 'they are never destroyed or retreated as a result of their own failed attacks' - but 'Bombarding Artillery units may voluntarily elect to suffer an "Attacker Retreat" combat result.'
corrections.folio_verbatim: When an attack fails, bombarding artillery (i.e., attacking from two hexes distant) suffer no ill effects: they are never destroyed or retreated as a result of their own failed attacks. Artillery units attacking from an adjacent position must suffer all the combat results of their attacks. Bombarding Artillery units may voluntarily elect to suffer an "Attacker Retreat" combat result.

evidence.crop_spec: page 1, frac x 0.7487-0.8707 (column 7, px 5217-6067), y 0.10-0.62; carries artillery cases (A)-(F) whole
evidence.negative_evidence: the substring 'volunt' occurs exactly once in the per-column OCR of the entire page (fix_p1_percol_ocr.txt, line 560), inside this sentence

corrections.gate_consequence: The only voluntary retreat on the sheet is the opt-in to an Ar RESULT. A free voluntary retreat outside a combat result would be movement, forbidden in a Combat Phase by p.1 TURNS OF PLAY case (B.). Note that because the 2nd Ed gives the victorious player the retreat direction, an opted-in Ar hands the direction choice to the defender.

corrections.rule_ref: 2nd Ed p.5, run-in DISRUPTION paragraph inside RETREAT AND ADVANCE, British/Prussian aid
corrections.was: DISRUPTION presented in a section whose stated source is 'p. 1 (rules columns) and p. 5 (charts)', with no indication which carries it.
corrections.now: DISRUPTION is printed exactly once in the entire 2nd Edition folio: on page 5, as a run-in bold heading inside the Retreat and Advance block on the British/Prussian half. It is not on the rules sheet. A 'which page carries what' note was added to the section 3 header.

evidence.negative_evidence: own 2x per-column OCR of all eight columns of page 1 (fix_p1_percol_ocr.txt, 24516 chars): count('disrupt') = 0, count('safe') = 0, count('chain-reaction') = 0

corrections.gate_consequence: An encoder working from the rules columns alone ships the 2nd Edition with no disruption rule and no retreat rule and does not notice. Citing to the wrong page also makes the next reader's verification fail for the wrong reason.

corrections.class: paraphrase that widened a printed trigger
corrections.was: If the only safe hex available to a retreating unit is already occupied by an uninvolved friendly unit, that unit is displaced; where no path remains, 'the unit which was forced to retreat as a result of combat is ELIMINATED instead.'
corrections.now: The full paragraph is quoted verbatim, and the trigger is stated as printed: the elimination fires when the DISPLACEMENT of the uninvolved unit could only be made into Enemy units, Zones of Control or woods. In that case the uninvolved unit stays put and the original retreating unit dies.
corrections.folio_verbatim: DISRUPTION: If the only "safe" hex available to the retreating unit is one which is already occupied by another, uninvolved Friendly unit, then the uninvolved unit is "disrupted" (pushed out of its hex) by the retreating unit. The uninvolved unit is moved back (by the victorious Player) as if it were retreating, and its position is taken by the retreating unit. The disrupted unit itself may not be forced into Enemy units or Zones of Control or woods. If this would be the only path of retreat available, then the uninvolved unit is NOT disrupted: It stays in its original position and the unit which was forced to retreat as a result of combat is ELIMINATED instead. Disrupted units can themselves disrupt other Friendly units in a sort of "chain-reaction" of disruption, if that is the only safe path of retreat open to them. Disrupted artillery units may NOT fire in the Combat Phase in which they were disrupted.

evidence.crop_spec: page 5, frac x 0.000-0.215, y 0.150-0.340 and y 0.320-0.510, rotate 90; the paragraph opens at the foot of one printed column and continues at the head of the next

corrections.gate_consequence: A unit that survives under the printed rule dies under the paraphrase, and vice versa, in ordinary crowded positions. Also closes the PREP-1 'bridging clause unresolved' flag: the unresolved connective was the 'moved back ... as if it were retreating' / 'may not be forced into' pair, now read at 6x.
still_undefined_in_print: whether the displacement may be pushed off the map - that bar is listed for retreats and omitted from the disruption sentence
whether the bare 'woods' means all Woods hexes or only the 'non-Road Woods' named two sentences earlier
'moved back ... as if it were retreating' - back relative to what, since the disrupted unit fought no combat
which unit dies when a chain-reaction fails at depth N

corrections.rule_ref: 2nd Ed p.5, EXPLANATION OF RESULTS, both printed copies
corrections.was: A single normalised transcription, given once, implying the two printed copies are identical; the EX gloss stopped at '...made up only from units directly involved in that attack.'
corrections.now: The two copies are flagged as different settings of the same rules, and the EX entry's closing sentence is restored.

folio_verbatim.french_copy: AE= Attacker Eliminated: The attacking unit(s) is eliminated (destroyed) and is immediately removed from the map. ... EX= Exchange: ... Both side's losses are immediately removed from the map. A surviving attacking unit may then exercise the option to advance into the hex formerly occupied by the Defender. ... Dr= Defender Retreats ... DE= Defender Eliminated
folio_verbatim.british_prussian_copy: AE - Attacker Eliminated: The attacking unit(s) is (are) eliminated (destroyed) and is(are) immediately removed from the map. ... EX - Exchange: ... Both sides' losses are immediately removed from the map. A surviving attacking unit may then exercise the option to advance into the hex formerly occupied by the Defender. ... Dr - Defender Retreats ... DE - Defender Eliminated
differences: code/gloss separator: French '=' vs British/Prussian en dash
number agreement: French 'unit(s) is eliminated' vs British/Prussian 'unit(s) is(are) eliminated'
French copy prints 'Both side's losses' (printed typo, one copy only); British/Prussian prints 'Both sides' losses'

evidence.crop_spec: French copy: page 5 frac x 0.790-1.000, y 0.300-0.500, rotate 270. British/Prussian copy: frac x 0.000-0.215, y 0.150-0.340, rotate 90.

corrections.gate_consequence: 'The two printed copies agree cell for cell' is true of the CRT and false of this chart; it had been carried over silently. The restored clause is substantive: the 2nd Edition affirmatively permits an advance after an EX, which the document was silent on.

corrections.section: RULEBOOK_VERIFIED.md section 3 ('Retreat and advance' sourcing note) and new section 5 discrepancy D17
corrections.rule_ref: 2nd Ed p.1, whole sheet (negative finding); procedure carried by p.5 chart
corrections.class: addition - omission in the printed game, never recorded by this document
corrections.was: (absent) The document gave the retreat rules without saying where they are printed, and never recorded that page 1 has none.
corrections.now: The rules sheet contains no retreat procedure of any kind. Eleven occurrences of 'retreat' on page 1, all references to a retreat happening; none states who chooses direction, how far, which hexes are legal, or what happens when none is. The whole procedure is on the page-5 chart, British/Prussian half only. Recorded in section 3 and as source defect D17.

evidence.hit_lines: 308, 368, 369, 382, 472, 479, 509, 556, 561, 579, 658 - each read in context, each a reference to a retreat occurring

corrections.gate_consequence: Standing trap for any pipeline that treats 'the rulebook' as page 1. Classified as a defect of the ORIGINAL PUBLISHED GAME (component split / omission), registered as D17.

corrections.rule_ref: 2nd Ed p.1 col.4, MOVEMENT, case (K.) [rules_2nd_ed.json MOV-19]
corrections.class: addition - printed rule the document never mentioned
corrections.was: (absent) Movement case (K.) did not appear in the document at all.
corrections.now: Once a unit has been moved, and the Player's hand is taken from the piece, it may not be moved any further during that Player-Turn, not may it change its move without the consent of the opposing Player.
corrections.folio_verbatim: Once a unit has been moved, and the Player's hand is taken from the piece, it may not be moved any further during that Player-Turn, not may it change its move without the consent of the opposing Player.

evidence.printed_typo: 'not may it change' where the sense requires 'nor' - the third printed typo on this sheet, alongside 'extends' (NAW2-SD-1) and 'or it contains' (C3)

corrections.gate_consequence: Unenforceable as written - the trigger is physical and the escape is social. But it is the printed rule that governs whether an engine UNDO is legal: an undo is precisely 'changing a move', and this case makes it require the opponent's consent. Engine-policy question for Bruce, not a legality check.

corrections.rule_ref: 2nd Ed p.1 col.6 COMBAT case (H.) vs p.5 OPTIONAL ADVANCE block
corrections.was: A single merged, unattributed Optional-advance bullet, which a reader would take for rules-column text.
corrections.now: Per-sentence sourcing. The page-5 block is quoted for the ZOC, immediacy, never-forced, one-hex and no-MP statements; page 1 case (H.) is quoted separately and its narrower scope stated explicitly.

folio_verbatim.page1_case_H: Whenever, as a direct result of combat, an Enemy unit is thrown back (retreated) or removed from play (eliminated) the victorious unit may advance into the hex formerly occupied by the defeated force. The option to advance is exercised IMMEDIATELY. The advance may be made even if the advancing unit is still in an Enemy unit's Zone of Control. Retreating and advancing due to combat is not considered as part of regular Movement and is not counted as an expenditure of Movement Points.
folio_verbatim.page5_optional_advance: OPTIONAL ADVANCE: Whenever a hex is vacated as a result of combat, the victorious unit responsible for the Enemy elimination or retreat may advance into the vacated hex. This may be done even if the victorious unit is still in an Enemy Zone of Control and/or if the vacated hex is in an Enemy Zone of Control. The option to advance must be exercised immediately. A unit is never forced to advance. A unit may never advance more than one hex as a result of combat. Advances are not counted as regular Movement and therefore expend no Movement Points.

But the page-5 OPTIONAL ADVANCE block prints: 'This may be done even if the victorious unit is still in an Enemy Zone of Control and/or if the vacated hex is in an Enemy Zone of Control.' Section 3 of the document draws on p.1 AND p.5, so the sentence is sourced and correct.

rejected_after_verification.what_i_read: Both are printed as flat sentences in the page-5 OPTIONAL ADVANCE block: 'A unit is never forced to advance. A unit may never advance more than one hex as a result of combat.' They are not inferences.
